mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically different from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month predicts a contractionary demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are not statistically distinguishable from neutral periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly lower during triggered periods compared to baseline, or the trigger is met but returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the magnitude of negative returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 2% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an aggressive policy easing in recession, which historically coincides with a positive S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as risk appetite rebounds.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.5% AND GDPC1 quarterly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% coincident with a consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increase above 3% signals a tight labor market with inflationary pressure, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered months, or the trigger is met but returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% year-over-year, coupled with a decline in consumer spending growth (proxied by GDPC1), signals a shift from consumption to savings, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue growth slows.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change > 5% AND GDPC1 YoY change < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but returns are positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between monthly industrial production growth (INDPRO) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns; higher manufacturing activity is associated with improved earnings expectations and near-term equity gains.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO monthly change and S&P 500 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
